evidence: src/infrastructure/in-memory-order-repository.ts: class InMemoryOrderRepository implements OrderRepository and stores orders in a private Map<string, Order>, which is persistence and fits the infrastructure layer.
findById(id) returns this.orders.get(id), a plain lookup with no business logic.
findByState(state) filters on order.state === state, which is a query criterion and not a domain rule.
save(order) runs this.orders.set(order.id, order) and stores the order without validating it or changing its state.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: This file belongs to the infrastructure layer. Its only job is to persist and look up orders, which fits that layer. InMemoryOrderRepository stores orders in a Map and fills in the domain OrderRepository port with findById, findByState and save. findByState filters orders by matching state. That is a query criterion, the same kind of thing as a WHERE clause, not a business rule or invariant. The file has no state-transition logic, validation or pricing, and nothing else that belongs to the domain or application layer. It also has no presentation concerns.
